cases.comparison: Require observed TCP fallback, failed DNS query, unchanged trap, and continued shell execution.
cases.oracle: Independent UDP/TCP peer returns a truncated response, records TCP accept, then closes with an immediate reset; shell trap is inspected before and after.
cases.purpose: A TCP reset during fallback must not kill the shell or change its PIPE trap.
cases.script:
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/dns-tcp-reset-peer.py
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" peer.log 2>peer.err & peer=$!
trap 'kill "$peer" 2>/dev/null; wait "$peer" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
for ((i=0;i<100;i++)); do [ -s peer.log ] && break; sleep 0.05; done
[ -s peer.log ] || exit 98
printf 'nameserver 127.0.0.2\noptions attempts:1 timeout:1\n' > resolv.conf
export BASHDNS_SERVER_PORT=5349 BASHDNS_RESOLV_CONF="$PWD/resolv.conf"
trap 'echo unexpected-sigpipe' PIPE
trap -p PIPE > before.trap
if dns query example.test A -s 127.0.0.2 -t 1000 > query.out 2> query.err; then echo reset=wrongly-accepted; exit 1; else echo reset=rejected; fi
trap -p PIPE > after.trap
if /usr/bin/cmp -s before.trap after.trap; then echo signal-disposition=preserved; else echo signal-disposition=changed; exit 1; fi
wait "$peer" || exit 1
if [[ $(<peer.log) == *'udp-query'*'tcp-accepted'* ]]; then echo tcp-reset=observed; else echo tcp-reset=missing; exit 1; fi
echo shell=alive
